tasks.title: Implement C64 scaled camera tracking, tile culling, and background parallax
tasks.description:
## Outcome
Ensure that in C64 scaled mode (640x340 virtual viewport), the camera tracks Giana smoothly, the ground and floating blocks are vertically centered/visible, tile culling loops cover 40x22 tiles, and background clouds/parallax elements render without clipping or jitter.

## Scope
- In: Updating `STAGE_Draw()`, `BACKGROUND_ELEMENTS_Outdoors_Draw()`, and tile rendering loops in `STAGE_Draw.cpp` and `PLAYER_Draw.cpp` for virtual 640x340 camera dimensions.
- Out: UI toggle buttons and input handling.

## Implementation notes
- In `STAGE_Draw.cpp`:
  - Calculate `PC.StagePosX = PC.PosX - (virtualWidth / 2)` where `virtualWidth = (GV.ViewMode == VIEW_MODE_C64_SCALED) ? 640 : GV.Screen_Width`. Clamp to `[0, StageC64.StageWidthPixels - virtualWidth]`.
  - Calculate `PC.StagePosY`: For C64 scaled mode, vertical height is 340px (out of 480px stage height). Anchor vertical view so ground is at the bottom of the viewport (`PC.StagePosY = 480 - 340 = 140`), with vertical tracking only if Giana jumps high into upper tiers (`PC.PosY < 180`).
  - Adjust tile iteration bounds: Loop `x` up to `PC.StagePosX / 16 + (virtualWidth / 16) + 1` and `y` up to `StageC64.StageHeight`.
  - Cloud and outdoor element Y-offsets: adjust parallax divider and cloud coordinates so clouds drift across the upper sky portion.

## Assumptions
- In 640x340 virtual mode, visible horizontal tiles is 40 (640/16) and visible vertical tiles is 21.25 (340/16).
- Ground is 5 tiles high at the bottom of the 30-tile stage, placing ground level cleanly at rows 25-29.

beadsSync.closeReason: Implemented 640x340 C64 viewport scaling, camera tracking, options toggle, V hotkey, persistence, and tests

tasks.title: Add 640x340 render target and view scaling engine infrastructure
tasks.description:
## Outcome
Provide the core render-target infrastructure and engine definitions so the gameplay rendering pipeline can switch between 1:1 native 320x170 and 0.5x scaled 640x340 virtual framebuffer modes.

## Scope
- In: `VIEW_MODE_1X_ZOOMED` and `VIEW_MODE_C64_SCALED` constants in `GAME_ENVIRONMENT.h`; `GV.ViewMode` field; 640x340 `SDL_Texture` render target allocation and cleanup in `SYSTEM_SDL_init.cpp` and `SYSTEM_SDL_Close.cpp`; render pass redirection in `SYSTEM_Update_Screen.cpp`.
- Out: Camera adjustments (handled in Task 2) and UI toggles (handled in Task 3).

## Implementation notes
- In `GAME_ENVIRONMENT.h`: `#define VIEW_MODE_1X_ZOOMED 0`, `#define VIEW_MODE_C64_SCALED 1`, add `int ViewMode;` to `GameVariables_Type`.
- In `SYSTEM_SDL_init.cpp`: Allocate `gameplayTargetTexture = SDL_CreateTexture(gRenderer, SDL_PIXELFORMAT_RGBA8888, SDL_TEXTUREACCESS_TARGET, 640, 340);` and set nearest-neighbor scale quality.
- In `SYSTEM_Update_Screen.cpp`: When `GV.ViewMode == VIEW_MODE_C64_SCALED`, direct renderer target to `gameplayTargetTexture`, clear, render stage/player/enemies/sprites, restore target to NULL, blit `gameplayTargetTexture` to screen (`320x170`), and then draw `STAGE_Interface_Draw()` directly on screen.

## Assumptions
- Target texture uses 640x340 (exact 2:1 ratio to 320x170) to allow clean integer downsampling.

tasks.title: Implement C64-authentic viewport scaling with in-game toggle
tasks.description:
## Outcome
Allow Cardputer ZERO players to view the full vertical stage layout (ground, floating question blocks, and clouds simultaneously) by providing an authentic Commodore 64 0.5x scaled viewport mode alongside the 1:1 zoomed mode, with seamless toggling in settings and during gameplay.

## Scope
- In: 640x340 virtual render target downscaled to 320x170 via SDL2; C64 scaled camera tracking and tile culling; in-game Options menu toggle (`VIEW: C64 (0.5X)` vs `VIEW: 1:1 (ZOOM)`); in-game quick toggle hotkey (`V` key); binary options persistence in `SavedOptions`; razor-sharp native 320x170 HUD overlay across both modes.
- Out: Modifying on-disk sprite texture PNGs, physics equations, collision tile routines, or level file formats.

## Interaction / UX
- Options screen contains a toggle button to switch between `VIEW: C64 (0.5X)` and `VIEW: 1:1 (ZOOM)`.
- Pressing `V` key during active gameplay flips between the two view modes immediately with an audio click.
- The 1-line HUD (score, coins, lives, stage, time) and status overlays (PAUSED, Low Battery) render directly on top at native 320x170 for maximum legibility.

## Implementation notes
- Engine state: `GV.ViewMode` (`VIEW_MODE_1X_ZOOMED`, `VIEW_MODE_C64_SCALED`) in `GAME_ENVIRONMENT.h`.
- Render target: 640x340 `SDL_Texture` created with `SDL_TEXTUREACCESS_TARGET` in `SYSTEM_SDL_init.cpp`.
- Viewport blit: In `SYSTEM_Update_Screen.cpp`, route stage, player, enemies, and sprites to target texture in C64 mode, blit scaled to display, and render HUD directly on framebuffer.
- Camera: In `STAGE_Draw.cpp`, calculate horizontal and vertical camera offsets for 640x340 virtual viewport.
- Persistence: Store `GV.ViewMode` in `SavedOptions.Var4` in `GAME_ENVIRONMENT.cpp`.

## Assumptions
- Default view mode on Cardputer ZERO will be `VIEW_MODE_C64_SCALED` to provide authentic retro C64 proportions, while preserving the user's ability to switch to `VIEW_MODE_1X_ZOOMED`.
- Nearest-neighbor texture filtering is used during blitting to preserve crisp pixel art aesthetics.

beadsSync.closeReason: Implemented 640x340 C64 viewport scaling, camera tracking, options toggle, V hotkey, persistence, and tests
